title: Disgust, Shame and Soapy Water: Tests of Novel Interventions to Promote Safe Water and Hygiene
venue: Journal of the Association of Environmental and Resource Economists
abstract: Lack of access to clean water is among the most pressing environmental problems in developing countries, where diarrheal disease kills nearly 700,000 children per year. While inexpensive and effective practices such as chlorination and hand washing with soap exist, efforts to motivate their use by emphasizing health benefits have seen only limited success. This paper measures the effect of messages appealing to negative emotions (disgust at consumption of human feces) and social pressure (shame at being seen consuming human feces) on hand-washing behavior and use of and willingness to pay for water chlorination among residents of slum compounds in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Neither the traditional, health-based message nor the new disgust-and-shame message led to high levels of chlorination during a free trial, nor to high willingness to pay for the chlorine at the end of the free trial. Provision of low-cost hand-washing facilities did increase hand washing, although the effect size is modest.
abstract_zh: 缺乏清洁水源是发展中国家面临的最紧迫的环境问题之一，那里每年有近 70 万名儿童因腹泻病而死亡。尽管氯化消毒和使用肥皂洗手等廉价而有效的做法已经存在，但通过强调健康益处来推动这些做法的努力收效有限。本文测量了诉诸负面情绪（对食用人类粪便的厌恶）和社会压力（因被看到食用人类粪便而感到羞耻）的信息，对孟加拉国达卡贫民窟居民洗手行为、氯化消毒的使用以及对氯消毒剂支付意愿的影响。无论是传统的以健康为基础的信息，还是新的厌恶与羞耻信息，在免费试用期间都没有带来较高的氯化消毒水平，试用期结束时对氯的支付意愿也不高。提供低成本洗手设施确实增加了洗手行为，但效应规模适中。

title: The Pursuit of Balance in Sequential Randomized Trials
Encouraging Sanitation Investment in the Developing World: A Cluster-Randomized Trial
abstract: Poor sanitation contributes to morbidity and mortality in the developing world, but there is disagreement on what policies can increase sanitation coverage. To measure the effects of alternative policies on investment in hygienic latrines, we assigned 380 communities in rural Bangladesh to different marketing treatments-community motivation and information; subsidies; a supply-side market access intervention; and a control-in a cluster-randomized trial. Community motivation alone did not increase hygienic latrine ownership (+1.6 percentage points, P = 0.43), nor did the supply-side intervention (+0.3 percentage points, P = 0.90). Subsidies to the majority of the landless poor increased ownership among subsidized households (+22.0 percentage points, P < 0.001) and their unsubsidized neighbors (+8.5 percentage points, P = 0.001), which suggests that investment decisions are interlinked across neighbors. Subsidies also reduced open defecation by 14 percentage points (P < 0.001).
abstract_zh: 卫生条件不佳导致发展中国家的发病率和死亡率上升，但对于何种政策能够提高卫生设施覆盖率，目前仍存在分歧。为了测量不同政策对卫生厕所投资的效果，我们在孟加拉国农村将 380 个社区随机分配至不同的营销处理组：社区动员与信息提供组、补贴组、供给侧市场准入干预组，以及对照组，开展了整群随机试验。仅有社区动员并未提高卫生厕所的拥有率（+1.6 个百分点，P = 0.43），供给侧干预同样没有效果（+0.3 个百分点，P = 0.90）。向大多数无地贫困者提供补贴，提高了获得补贴家庭的拥有率（+22.0 个百分点，P < 0.001），也提高了其未获补贴邻居的拥有率（+8.5 个百分点，P = 0.001），这表明投资决策在邻里之间是相互关联的。补贴还使露天排便减少了 14 个百分点（P < 0.001）。

title: Satellites, Self-reports, and Submersion: Exposure to Floods in Bangladesh
venue: American Economic Review: Papers and Proceedings
abstract: A burgeoning “Climate-Economy” literature has uncovered many effects of changes in temperature and precipitation on economic activity, but has made considerably less progress in modeling the effects of other associated phenomena, like natural disasters. We develop new, objective data on floods, focusing on Bangladesh. We show that rainfall and self-reported exposure are weak proxies for true flood exposure. These data allow us to study adaptation, giving accurate measures of both long-term averages and short term variation in exposure. This is important in studying climate change impacts, as people will not only experience new exposures, but also experience them differently.
abstract_zh: 大量“气候-经济”文献揭示了气温和降水变化对经济活动的诸多影响，但在建模其他相关现象（如自然灾害）的影响方面进展相对较少。我们以孟加拉国为研究对象，构建了关于洪水的新的客观数据。我们发现，降雨量和自我报告的暴露程度都是真实洪水暴露的较弱代理指标。这些数据使我们能够研究适应行为，并准确衡量长期平均暴露水平和短期暴露波动。这对于研究气候变化影响至关重要，因为人们不仅会面临新的暴露，还会以不同的方式经历这些暴露。

title: Routine Disasters: Floods, Human Capital and Adaptation in Bangladesh
